articles.title: The Plan: Major League Soccer Scores Big With Global HQ Design at Vornado’s 2 Penn
articles.narrative: Major League Soccer (MLS) has opened its new 126,000-square-foot global headquarters at Vornado Realty Trust's 2 Penn Plaza in Midtown Manhattan. Designed by TPG Architecture, the two-floor office space blends the excitement of a stadium experience with a sense of community and neighborhood connectivity. The design incorporates elements like a player's tunnel-inspired entrance, digital scoreboards, and a central hub for monitoring live matches, while also providing tranquil "neighborhoods" for focused work and collaboration.

data_points.address: 2 Penn Plaza, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: The office design incorporates a stadium-like entrance, digital scoreboards, and a central hub for monitoring live matches, alongside quieter 'neighborhood' workspaces.

articles.title: Developer Wolfe Landau Buys FiDi Redevelopment Site for $35M
articles.narrative: Wolfe Landau's Peninim Water has acquired two adjacent Financial District lots at 78 Pearl Street and 46-48 Water Street in New York City for $35 million. The irregularly-shaped, block-through site spans over 10,000 square feet and includes a vacant lot and an empty mixed-use building. The properties were sold by a consortium including the Milstein Organization, Swig Company, and Weiler Arnow Management, who had owned the parcels since the 1970s and 80s.

data_points.address: 78 Pearl Street and 46-48 Water Street, New York City, NY
data_points.project_notes: The Water Street property is being prepared for demolition.

articles.title: London Nightclub Operator Buys 675 Hudson Street for $100M
articles.narrative: London-based club operator Caprice Holdings has acquired the five-story Herring Building at 675 Hudson Street in New York City for $100 million from Aurora Capital Associates. The buyer plans to convert the historic 19th-century property into a private club, a New York outpost of its Annabel's brand, pending approval from the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission for proposed alterations including a rooftop addition. HSBC provided $165 million in financing for the acquisition.

data_points.address: 675 Hudson Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Historic 19th-century building in the Meatpacking District, landmarked property.
data_points.project_notes: Aurora Capital Associates previously acquired the property in 2023 for $50 million. Proposed rooftop addition design by BKSK Architects has faced reservations from the Landmarks Preservation Commission.

articles.title: PGIM Hires David Blum as Managing Director of Commercial Real Estate Credit
Can One Giant Project Change the Narrative Around Downtown Los Angeles?
articles.narrative: The Los Angeles City Council has approved the $2 billion Fourth & Central mixed-use megadevelopment, a 7.6-acre project that will bring 1,589 residences, offices, and retail to downtown. This approval is seen as a crucial signal of optimism for the downtown development market, particularly for housing, despite previous delays and waning institutional sentiment. Industry experts believe the project's green light, following a period of significant property valuation cuts, will encourage further creative development and redevelopment by reducing entitlement risk and demonstrating the city's willingness to approve large-scale density.

data_points.address: 5606 S Figueroa St, Los Angeles, CA
data_points.notable_features: The project will consist of 10 buildings, with nearly one in seven units designated as affordable.
data_points.project_notes: The Rauch family will relocate their existing cold-storage buildings from the site. The project's approval is seen as a positive outcome of the city's Downtown 2040 Plan and the state's SB 79 law, which streamline development and increase density bonuses.

companies_people.label: OWNER

articles.market_intelligence: Downtown Los Angeles land values have seen steep cuts from pre-pandemic levels, with sale comps like Bank of America Plaza and Aon Center trading significantly lower than the neighborhood average of $450 per square foot. The city's Downtown 2040 Plan has increased the portion of downtown allowing by-right development from 30 percent to 60 percent, and the recently approved state law SB 79 increases density bonuses for transit-oriented development, covering a significant portion of downtown. The city's updated Adaptive Reuse Ordinance also offers incentives for redeveloping older buildings.

articles.title: LITEON to Invest $919M in Metro Dallas Manufacturing Campus, Create 600 Jobs
articles.narrative: LITEON Technology Corp., a provider of power management and AI infrastructure solutions, has acquired over 650,000 square feet of existing industrial space within Core5 Logistics Center in McKinney, Texas. The company plans to invest $919 million in capital improvements to establish a new manufacturing campus, which is expected to create approximately 600 new jobs. This significant investment was facilitated through collaboration with the City of McKinney and the McKinney Economic Development Corp., and is anticipated to bolster the city's high-tech employer base and tax revenue.

data_points.notable_features: Located within a newly developed industrial park north of Dallas.
data_points.project_notes: Investment includes capital improvements and is expected to create 600 new jobs.

articles.title: Joint Venture Buys Two Student Housing Communities Totaling 1,128 Beds Near Texas A&M University
articles.narrative: A joint venture between PCCP LLC and The Dinerstein Cos. has acquired two adjacent student housing communities near Texas A&M University in College Station. The properties, now rebranded as Sterling College Station, offer a combined 1,128 beds across 350 units. The community features a variety of amenities including a pool, fitness center, and sports courts.

data_points.notable_features: Garden- and cottage-style units with one-, two-, and four-bedroom configurations. Amenities include a pool, fitness center, business center with cybercafé, private study rooms, basketball and beach volleyball courts, outdoor grilling stations, and a clubhouse with a community kitchen, game lounge, and pool tables.
data_points.project_notes: Formerly known as 2818 Apartments and Parkway Place, the two adjacent communities have been combined and rebranded.

articles.title: Haven Housing Acquires 309-Unit Apartment Community in Kyle, Texas
articles.narrative: California-based investment firm Haven Housing has acquired Hays Park Apartments, a 309-unit multifamily community in Kyle, Texas. The garden-style property features a mix of one- and two-bedroom units and offers amenities such as a clubhouse, two pools, a fitness center with yoga studios, and a business center. Walker and Dunlop brokered the transaction.

data_points.notable_features: Garden-style property with a clubhouse, two pools, fitness center with yoga studios, and a business center.

articles.title: Northmarq Arranges Refinancing of 199-Unit Apartment Complex in Corpus Christi
articles.narrative: Northmarq has arranged a fixed-rate, nonrecourse loan for the refinancing of Wood River Apartments, a 199-unit multifamily complex in Corpus Christi. The loan carries a five-year term. The property, built in 1983, features one-, two-, and three-bedroom units across 17 buildings, along with amenities such as a pool and pet facilities.

data_points.address: 4021 Wood River Dr, Corpus Christi, TX
data_points.notable_features: Features a pool and pet facilities.
data_points.project_notes: Nonrecourse loan with a five-year term and fixed interest rate.

articles.title: Avison Young Brokers $17.9M Sale of Apartment Building in Norwalk, Connecticut
articles.narrative: Avison Young has brokered the sale of The Stonefield, a 55-unit apartment building in Norwalk, Connecticut, for $17.9 million. The seller was developer EDG Properties, and the buyer was a group of local investors utilizing a 1031 exchange.

data_points.project_notes: Buyer completed a 1031 exchange.

articles.title: The good news in Chicago’s office market? Positive net absorption and plans for a new office tower downtown
articles.narrative: The Chicago office market is showing signs of improvement, with downtown experiencing positive direct net absorption for the first time since 2023 and plans for a new office tower groundbreaking. The suburban market also recorded its strongest first-half net absorption since 2018. Demand for turnkey and high-quality space is a key driver, with move-in-ready suites accounting for a significant portion of leasing activity in both the CBD and suburbs. While overall vacancy remains high, particularly for Class A space, developers are regaining confidence, and the market is on track for positive net absorption by year-end.

people.name: Neil Bouhan
people.title: senior managing director, research and communications

articles.market_intelligence: Downtown Chicago's CBD office market posted direct net absorption of 585,646 square feet in Q2, a significant improvement from -345,914 square feet in Q1. Leasing velocity declined in H1 2026, with 1.2 million square feet of direct deals in Q2 compared to 1.9 million square feet in Q1. Demand for turnkey space is growing, accounting for 36.7% of year-to-date leasing in the CBD (up from 20.6% in 2023) and over 50% in the suburbs. Class A vacancy in the CBD is nearly 22%. Suburban Chicago's office market saw over 2 million square feet leased in H1 2026, with over half a million square feet of net positive absorption. The average new lease size in the suburbs was 27,000 square feet, a 69% increase from H2 2025. Suburban investment sales volume year-to-date is $112 million, with average pricing at $131 per square foot, up from $49 per square foot at year-end 2025.

articles.title: CBRE brokers sale of 295-unit multifamily property in Carmel
articles.narrative: CBRE has brokered the sale of The Signature at Carmel, a 295-unit multifamily property in Carmel, Indiana. The recently built property offers a mix of studio, one, and two-bedroom floorplans with a strong amenity package.

data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a resort-style swimming pool, fitness center, co-working spaces, in-unit washers/dryers, climate-controlled parking garage, pickleball court, pet spa, and private patios/balconies. Located minutes south of U.S. Route 31 with access to retail, entertainment, recreation, and public parks.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap facilitates sale of 53,812-square-foot self-storage facility in Athens
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has facilitated the sale of North Loop Mini Warehouses, a 53,812-square-foot self-storage facility in Athens, TX. The property, which was inherited by a family, was sold to a California-based private investor looking to expand their existing self-storage portfolio in East Texas. The transaction highlights the continued demand for self-storage assets in growing markets and opportunities for operational improvements.

data_points.project_notes: The property was previously operated as a family-owned self-storage facility before ownership transitioned to relatives who inherited the asset.

articles.title: Kiser Group negotiates sale of 11-unit mixed-use property in Chicago’s Wicker Park neighborhood
articles.narrative: Kiser Group recently brokered the sale of an 11-unit mixed-use property in Chicago's Wicker Park neighborhood for $3.88 million. The fully occupied asset, comprising three commercial spaces and eight residential apartments, underwent a comprehensive gut renovation in 2020, featuring updated building systems and high-end finishes. Its prime location near the Milwaukee and Damen corridor, coupled with its stabilized occupancy and recent upgrades, attracted substantial investor interest.

data_points.notable_features: Gut-renovated in 2020 with updated plumbing, electrical, roof, windows, and interiors; residential units feature high-end finishes and individual mechanical systems. Located near Wicker Park's Milwaukee and Damen corridor.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap brokers sale of four-suite retail property in Mundelein
articles.narrative: A four-suite retail property anchored by LA Fitness in Mundelein, Illinois, has been sold for $13.976 million. Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale and arranged $9.783 million in acquisition financing for the out-of-state buyer, who was completing a 1031-exchange. The property, built in 2019, is part of the larger Townline Square Shopping Center.

data_points.notable_features: Anchored by LA Fitness, located at a signalized intersection with high traffic counts, and minutes from the $250 million redevelopment of Hawthorn Mall.
data_points.project_notes: The buyer was in a 1031-exchange.

articles.title: Greystar accused of violating fair housing laws
articles.narrative: Greystar, the nation's largest apartment landlord, faces accusations from the watchdog group Housing Rights Initiative for systematically violating state fair housing laws by denying Section 8 housing vouchers. The group conducted a "tester" program across multiple states, alleging over 100 violations in jurisdictions where source-of-income discrimination is illegal. Greystar stated it provides employee training and is committed to fair housing practices, while the Housing Rights Initiative executive director described the alleged violations as unprecedented in scale.

articles.title: Arizona price record: Paradise Valley estate sells for $40M
articles.narrative: A 20,900-square-foot estate in Paradise Valley, Arizona, sold for over $40.2 million in an all-cash transaction, setting a new record for the most expensive home sale in state history. The property, designed by Candelaria Design and built by Arcadia Custom Builders, features extensive luxury amenities. The sale highlights the resilient demand for high-end luxury homes in the Phoenix metro area, driven by out-of-state cash buyers, with prices for top-tier properties continuing to appreciate.

data_points.address: 5531 East Mockingbird Lane, Paradise Valley, AZ
data_points.notable_features: Amenities include a 38-car garage, an underground go-kart track, a gun range, a salon and spa, a detached guest house, and a casita.

articles.market_intelligence: Home prices in the Phoenix metro's highest-priced quartile have appreciated 6.2 percent year over year, while lower-priced segments saw changes between 0 and 1.9 percent. The listing agent noted that $2,000 per square foot is becoming the new standard for top-tier homes.

articles.title: Zeckondorf family accuses supermarket moguls of selling pilfered art
articles.narrative: The Zeckendorf family, prominent New York office developers, has filed a lawsuit against the heirs of Robert and Patricia Weis, who control Weis Markets, alleging they sold a painting stolen from the Zeckendorf patriarch's estate. The abstract work by Pierre Soulages, "Peinture 161 x 200 cm, 14 novembre 1958," was auctioned at Christie's New York for $4.95 million. The Zeckendorfs are seeking the proceeds from the sale, claiming the painting was stolen around 1977 and that the Weis family's acquisition documents show inconsistencies.

articles.title: Court rejects REBNY’s FARE Act appeal
articles.narrative: A federal appeals court has rejected the Real Estate Board of New York's (REBNY) appeal to revive key claims against the city's Fairness in Apartment Rental Expenses (FARE) Act. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirmed a lower court's dismissal of REBNY's claims that the FARE Act violates the First Amendment and is preempted by state law. The court also upheld the denial of REBNY's request to prevent the law from taking effect during the lawsuit. REBNY expressed disappointment and plans to explore further legal challenges against the law, which shifts the responsibility for paying broker fees from tenants to landlords.

data_points.project_notes: The FARE Act went into effect in June 2025. REBNY's claim against existing contracts (tenant-pays listing agreements signed before December 13, 2024, and active after the FARE Act) remains intact.

articles.title: Defense Department signs 10-year lease for Long Island office
articles.narrative: The government agency formerly known as the Department of Defense has signed a 10-year lease for 23,600 square feet at 1 Old Country Road in Carle Place, NY. The five-story office building, owned by DBD Realty Group, recently underwent a $22 million renovation. This significant lease contributes to the property's strong demand from institutional and government tenants, which value its scale, infrastructure, and accessibility.

data_points.address: 1 Old Country Road, Carle Place, NY
data_points.notable_features: The 320,000-square-foot property recently underwent a $22 million renovation, including updates to its facade, windows, lobby, bathrooms, wiring, sprinkler systems, and technology infrastructure.

articles.title: Hochul orders 1-year ban on large data center construction
articles.narrative: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has issued a one-year moratorium on the construction of large data centers exceeding 50 megawatts that have not yet received permits. This executive order aims to allow the state to develop environmental assessments, establish consistent standards for data center operations, and create rules for their energy provision. The move comes amid public concern over the environmental and financial impacts of hyperscale facilities, with the governor emphasizing the need to address potential utility bill hikes and resource depletion. The state is also exploring ways to extract more benefits from data center development, including a potential fund for grid investment and a review of sales tax exemptions.

articles.title: Housing Notes: Developers are in on the joke: Apologize later
articles.narrative: This article explores the unique mindset of Manhattan developers, characterized by their relentless pursuit of projects despite obstacles and a tendency to prioritize action over permission. The author, a real estate appraiser and former Columbia MSRED instructor, contrasts this aggressive approach with the more understated style of developers like Nathan Berman, currently undertaking an office-to-residential conversion. The piece uses the infamous "midnight demolition" by Harry Macklowe in 1985 as a prime example of a developer pushing legal and political boundaries to secure project value, ultimately resulting in criminal charges and a significant settlement, though the project itself later faced foreclosure. The author concludes by noting Macklowe's contrasting fondness for humor and warns against developers describing their projects as "art," citing Macklowe's 432 Park Avenue as an example.

data_points.project_notes: The Macklowe Hotel (now the Millennium Hotel) evolved from the 'midnight demolition' site five years after the event.

articles.title: PTM Partners, Peacock launch subsidy-free workforce housing platform
articles.narrative: PTM Partners and Peacock Capital have launched Inception Housing, a new platform focused on developing workforce housing in Florida without government subsidies. The platform aims to reduce development costs by managing design, construction, and material procurement in-house, utilizing standardized cold-formed steel construction to achieve significant savings in both cost and construction time. This approach allows Inception Housing to offer lower-cost rental units to middle-income earners, addressing the critical housing shortage in high-growth Florida markets.

data_points.project_notes: Inception Housing has nearly 1,600 units in its development pipeline.

articles.market_intelligence: South Florida has a housing shortage of at least 30,460 units, while the statewide shortage in Florida is approximately 120,850 units.

articles.title: Here’s how Florida’s aging condo stock fared post-Surfside
articles.narrative: A new report from Florida's Office of Program Policy Analysis and Government Accountability reveals that the majority of aging condo buildings requiring significant repairs post-Surfside collapse are concentrated in South Florida. The report, based on milestone inspections in 2024 and 2025, found 54 buildings were deemed unsafe or uninhabitable during that period, primarily in South Florida. Many condo owners in the region are struggling with the costs of mandated repairs and new reserve funding requirements, leading some to consider selling to developers or bulk buyers.

articles.title: Progress Residential scores $385M refi for resi portfolio amid federal housing act
articles.narrative: Progress Residential, a major owner of single-family rental homes and a subsidiary of Pretium Partners, secured a $384.7 million refinancing for a multi-state residential portfolio. The loan, provided by Goldman Sachs Mortgage Company, was backed by properties valued at $462.1 million, including 64 homes in Broward County, Florida. This refinancing occurred shortly before the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law, which aims to increase housing supply and limit large investors from acquiring additional existing single-family homes, though it does not restrict refinancing of current portfolios.

data_points.project_notes: The loan has an 83 percent loan-to-value ratio, with the total portfolio valued at $462.1 million. The Broward County portion of the portfolio includes 64 residential properties across 14 cities, valued at $71.7 million.

articles.market_intelligence: Broward County's median gross rent was $1,907 between 2020 and 2024. Florida is Progress Residential's largest market, with a presence in six regions. Invitation Homes generated $556 million in revenue from its Florida portfolio during the first nine months of last year, owning nearly 27,000 homes valued at about $4.2 billion. American Homes 4 Rent owns nearly 8,700 single-family homes in Florida with an estimated value of roughly $2.1 billion. Corporate ownership of Florida single-family homes was estimated at roughly 117,000 as of late 2024.

articles.title: TFG International expands to South Florida amid wealth migration
articles.narrative: Luxury real estate group TFG International is expanding its operations into South Florida, establishing a presence in Miami through ONE Sotheby's International Realty. This move creates a bi-coastal operation connecting the Los Angeles and South Florida markets, driven by the migration of wealthy Californians to the Sunshine State. The firm aims to serve its existing ultra-luxury clients who are acquiring homes in South Florida, with plans to recruit additional agents for other market segments. The expansion is a strategic response to the synergistic market dynamics between Los Angeles and Miami, fueled by Florida's lifestyle, business-friendly environment, and the potential impact of a proposed wealth tax in California.

articles.title: Dolphins out, superyachts in: David Martin’s marina plan at former Seaquarium getting underway
articles.narrative: Miami-Dade County and Terra Group are planning a significant redevelopment of the former Miami Seaquarium site on Virginia Key, proposing to construct what could become the county's largest marina. The project, which includes 325 boat slips (90 for superyachts) and a 500-boat dry stack, aims to transform the site into a premier marine destination. State regulators have raised concerns regarding the project's potential environmental impact on protected wetlands, coral, and water quality, requesting further details on dredging, waste management, and alternative designs. The county, which evicted the previous tenant due to animal welfare violations, tentatively agreed to lease the site to Terra Group, with a final lease agreement still under negotiation.

data_points.notable_features: Proposed marina includes 325 boat slips, with 90 accommodating yachts over 80 feet, a 500-boat dry stack, a fuel depot, and a wave break that doubles as a fishing pier.
data_points.project_notes: Miami-Dade County owns the land and evicted the previous tenant in 2024. The county is seeking to rezone the property and establish a special district for the marina. The project requires multiple regulatory approvals, including compliance with the county's Manatee Protection Plan and potential voter approval for changes within the Biscayne Bay Aquatic Preserve.

articles.title: Law firms double down at Chicago’s AMA Plaza amid foreclosure
articles.narrative: Two law firms, Latham & Watkins and Swanson, Martin & Bell, have adjusted their lease agreements at AMA Plaza in downtown Chicago. Latham & Watkins expanded its footprint by 35,274 square feet, bringing its total to 194,000 square feet, and extended its lease by seven years. Swanson, Martin & Bell downsized its space from 91,000 square feet to 56,760 square feet but extended its lease for 12 years. These commitments are a positive sign for the building, which is facing a $372 million foreclosure lawsuit and is being marketed for sale by a court-appointed receiver.

data_points.notable_features: Premium office space.
data_points.project_notes: Building is facing a $372 million foreclosure complaint filed in 2024. Previous owners acquired the building for $468 million in 2016.

articles.market_intelligence: Downtown Chicago office occupancy rates are showing slight recovery towards pre-pandemic norms. Downtown office buildings, on average, have a 72% occupancy rating.

articles.title: Johnson’s effort to reassert Chicago Housing Authority power stymied by City Council vote
articles.narrative: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson's attempt to appoint three new members to the Chicago Housing Authority (CHA) board was blocked by a split City Council vote. The mayor sought to replace three existing board members who had voted to appoint Keith Pettigrew as CHA president, a move Johnson opposed. This political maneuvering comes amidst a lawsuit challenging Pettigrew's appointment, which critics argue violated Illinois' Open Meetings Act.

articles.title: TIF funding for the 78 gets key approval for $425M for needed infrastructure
articles.narrative: The Chicago City Council Committee on Finance has approved a $425 million infrastructure funding deal for The 78, a large-scale mixed-use development in Chicago. The agreement involves repaying developer Related Midwest for project-supporting infrastructure through tax increment financing (TIF), including $287 million from the Canal/Congress TIF district. This public funding is crucial for updating roads and other infrastructure necessary for the project, which will also include a privately-funded stadium for the Chicago Fire soccer team. The deal is expected to reduce the developer's immediate need to generate new tax revenue, with the full City Council scheduled for a final vote.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a privately-funded stadium for the Chicago Fire Major League Soccer franchise, named McDonald's Park.
data_points.project_notes: Infrastructure funding of $425 million approved, with $287 million in TIF money from the Canal/Congress TIF district to be injected into the Roosevelt/Clark TIF district where The 78 is planned.

articles.title: Crow Holdings secures $380M refi deal for 1,500-unit apartment portfolio
articles.narrative: Crow Holdings secured a $380.2 million refinancing package from AllianceBernstein for a five-property multifamily portfolio totaling 1,549 units across Texas, Colorado, and Virginia. The properties, developed in partnership with Trammell Crow Residential and delivered between 2019 and 2023, are part of the firm's extensive Alexan apartment portfolio. This refinancing comes as multifamily markets, particularly in Texas, show signs of stabilization after a period of significant new supply and rent declines.

data_points.project_notes: Properties were delivered between 2019 and 2023.

articles.market_intelligence: Austin's rental rates for new leases were down 3.9 percent year over year at the end of June, an improvement from a 7.5 percent year-over-year drop in March.

articles.title: Dallas apartment pipeline gets a boost with pair of financing deals
articles.narrative: Two separate apartment projects in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex recently secured financing. Endeavor Real Estate obtained funding for Lucille, a 22-story luxury high-rise in Dallas's Uptown district, which will include 265 units and ground-floor retail. Separately, StreetLights Residential secured $54 million in equity financing for a 22-story apartment tower in Plano, part of The Park at Legacy redevelopment. Both projects are slated to begin construction later this summer, with the Endeavor project targeting a late 2028 completion.

articles.title: Texas’ top construction permits for the week ending July 14, 2026
articles.narrative: John Peter Smith Hospital is undertaking the largest construction project in Texas, a $300 million central utility plant in Fort Worth. The Houston Independent School District is developing a 216,000-square-foot career and technical center, while Amazon is building a 1.2 million-square-foot distribution center in Terrell. Additionally, the city of Dallas is renovating the Dallas Museum of Art, Schlosser Development is managing a tenant improvement project for Mission 42 Ventures in Austin, and SteriTek is upgrading its industrial facility in Lewisville with a new e-beam sterilization machine.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Austin area empire triples land holdings
articles.narrative: Entities associated with Elon Musk have significantly expanded their land holdings in Bastrop County, Texas, tripling their acreage to approximately 2,000 acres since May. The acquisitions, totaling about 1,360 acres in the last three months, are concentrated along FM 969, a corridor between Bastrop and Austin. While the specific plans for the newly acquired land remain undisclosed, the area is already home to Musk's Gigasat solar factory, and his various companies have established a substantial presence in the Austin region since 2020.

data_points.notable_features: Land holdings are concentrated along FM 969, a rural roadway between Bastrop and Austin.
data_points.project_notes: Total land holdings in Bastrop County for Musk-tied entities now total approximately 2,000 acres, up from 700 acres earlier in the year.

articles.title: Air taxi operator grows in Silicon Valley with 501K sf Morgan Hill lease
articles.narrative: Archer Aviation, an air taxi manufacturer, has significantly expanded its Silicon Valley footprint with a 501,000-square-foot industrial lease at the Cochrane Technology Center in Morgan Hill. This move supports the company's plans to ramp up production for its first passenger flights later this year and its expansion into military aircraft. The developer, Trammell Crow Company, completed the five-building complex in 2024, anticipating increased demand for industrial space in south Santa Clara County.

data_points.address: 49X3+98, 18225 De Paul Dr, Morgan Hill, CA
data_points.notable_features: Five-building complex designed to serve manufacturing jobs in south Santa Clara County.

articles.title: Oakland officials approve $125M sale of Coliseum, arena properties
articles.narrative: Oakland officials have approved the sale of the city's stake in the Oakland Coliseum and adjacent Oakland Arena to Oakland Acquisition Company, a partnership between Loop Capital and the African American Sports and Entertainment Group, for $125 million. The transaction, which includes a deferred payment structure over seven years, aims to relieve the city of the financial burden of maintaining the vacant sports complex. A portion of the property, the arena parcel, will be acquired by Oak View Group, which plans to redevelop the 112-acre site into a mixed-use district featuring entertainment, retail, commercial, and residential components. The buyers envision the arena thriving as a concert and event venue, even without a major league sports tenant.

data_points.notable_features: Site is located near the city's airport and freeway network.
data_points.project_notes: Alameda County, which owns 50% of the property, negotiated a parallel agreement to sell its share for $115 million under similar deferred-payment terms. The city will receive $50 million when the arena sale closes, with most of the Coliseum site payment deferred over seven years. Buyers will pay $60 million for the stadium parcel in installments, plus an additional $15 million once development reaches the building permit stage. The city will also receive 6% of ticket revenue from both venues.

articles.title: Out with the old, in with the new: SF considers pulling Prop M allocations from inactive developers
articles.narrative: San Francisco is moving to revoke Proposition M office allocations from developers who have stalled on commercial projects, aiming to free up valuable development rights and accelerate downtown's recovery. The policy change, outlined by the San Francisco Planning Department Director, would immediately impact projects with little progress and give developers who proposed community benefits up to 18 months to secure building permits before forfeiture. This initiative is part of Mayor Daniel Lurie's broader strategy to prevent developers from indefinitely holding entitlements, especially as the Prop M pipeline has significantly tightened due to a 2020 measure linking office allocations to affordable housing production.

articles.title: A Buffett protege said to have bet nearly $49M on Union Square retail
articles.narrative: A Delaware corporation, Silver Gate Property II LLC, an affiliate of investor Ian Jacobs, acquired the four-story retail and office building at 180 Post Street in San Francisco for $48.5 million. The 39,000-square-foot property, anchored by a long-term lease with Bulgari, was sold by Grosvenor Americas, which had owned the building for three decades. This acquisition is part of Jacobs' ongoing strategy to invest in distressed commercial properties in downtown San Francisco, particularly around Union Square, reflecting a vote of confidence in the city's luxury retail sector despite broader challenges.

data_points.notable_features: Anchored by a long-term lease with LVMH-owned Italian jeweler Bulgari.

articles.market_intelligence: Overall vacancy in Union Square fell from 22.8 percent in Q2 2025 to 20 percent in Q2 2026, with monthly visitors increasing almost 10 percent year over year. The Union Square shopping district generated 13 percent of San Francisco's sales tax revenue before the pandemic.

articles.title: Garden-Style Apartments Go for $78M in North County San Diego
articles.narrative: 29th Street Capital has sold Sunterra, a 240-unit garden-style multifamily community in Oceanside, CA, for $77.5 million. The property, built in 1975, is situated on 14.24 acres and offers a mix of amenities, with approximately 70% of its units already renovated. The sale attracted significant investor interest due to its scale and coastal location, presenting an opportunity in a supply-constrained market with strong fundamentals and sustained renter demand.

data_points.notable_features: Low-density, garden-style apartment community with a resort-style pool, fitness center, and landscaped courtyards. Approximately 70% of units have been renovated.

articles.title: Related Beal Plans Complete Upgrade, Renovation of Salem Affordable Housing
articles.narrative: Related Beal, in partnership with Related Affordable, the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, and MassHousing, is undertaking a comprehensive $38 million renovation of the 250-unit Loring Towers affordable housing community in Salem, MA. The multi-phased project, set to begin in August and conclude by 2028, will extend the property's affordability through 2056, demonstrating a long-term commitment to the community and its residents. The renovation includes in-unit upgrades, common area improvements, and new amenities like a basketball court and children's playground.

data_points.notable_features: Includes a new basketball court and children's playground.
data_points.project_notes: Renovation extends long-term affordability to 2056.

articles.title: Slatt Capital Arranges Life Company Loan for Rohnert Park Offices
articles.narrative: Slatt Capital secured a $12 million non-recourse acquisition loan for a 68,094-square-foot multi-tenant office building in Rohnert Park, CA. The financing, provided by The Standard, features a staggered term and a 30-year amortization schedule, offering the buyer long-term permanent debt for the acquisition. This transaction highlights the lender's confidence in the stabilized asset's location, occupancy, and sponsorship, particularly in a challenging office lending market where non-recourse terms are increasingly selective.

data_points.address: 5900 State Farm Dr, Rohnert Park, CA
data_points.notable_features: Multi-tenant office building with a diversified rent roll.
data_points.project_notes: Non-recourse acquisition loan with a staggered term and 30-year amortization schedule.

articles.title: Revealed: The Banks Powering Private Credit's CRE Lending Boom
articles.narrative: This article analyzes the growing trend of traditional banks providing 'back leverage' to private credit firms, enabling them to expand their real estate lending activities. As regulatory constraints and past downturns have shifted banks away from direct lending, they are increasingly partnering with private credit funds through structures like warehouse lines, subscription facilities, and repurchase agreements. This symbiotic relationship allows banks to reduce their direct risk while still profiting from real estate debt, and it enables private credit firms to magnify their lending capabilities and lower their borrowing costs. The article highlights how major U.S. banks, including Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Citibank, dominate this space, each with distinct strategies, while smaller and digital banks like Axos Financial and Stifel Bank also play significant roles, often forming exclusive relationships with private lenders.

articles.title: Data Center Firms DataBank, EdgeCore Reportedly Courting Buyers
articles.narrative: Several prominent data center firms, including DataBank and EdgeCore, are reportedly exploring the sale of ownership stakes in their companies, driven by record demand and high valuations in the sector. DataBank, a Dallas-based operator with a significant U.S. and UK presence, is considering a sale of a majority stake that could reach $25 billion. EdgeCore, backed by Partners Group, is also seeking offers for a stake in its hyperscale-focused portfolio. This trend reflects a broader increase in data center operator mergers and acquisitions, with private equity firms expected to be key buyers in these platform-level transactions.
articles.market_intelligence: Data center M&A activity more than doubled last year, surpassing $60 billion, indicating a strong market for platform-level transactions.

articles.title: Lincoln Property Buys Charlotte Developer In Bid To Boost Deals
articles.narrative: Lincoln Property Co. has acquired Charlotte-based developer The Spectrum Cos., a move designed to significantly expand Lincoln's presence across the Carolinas and into northern and central Florida's multifamily sector. The acquisition merges Spectrum's substantial multifamily development expertise and portfolio with Lincoln's existing platform, aiming to boost the combined firm's development and acquisition pipeline. Executives from both companies emphasized the complementary nature of their portfolios, particularly Spectrum's strong focus on multifamily projects, which will enhance Lincoln's regional growth strategy.

data_points.project_notes: Spectrum's 43 employees will relocate to Lincoln's headquarters at Piedmont Town Center.

articles.market_intelligence: Charlotte is considered one of the most attractive markets for investors, according to CBRE's 2026 North America Investor Intentions Survey. The multifamily market in Charlotte is maintaining stronger demand fundamentals than most peer markets, with a 6.2% vacancy rate in Q1 indicating demand has absorbed new supply.

articles.title: Greystar Accused By Watchdog Of Discriminating Against Section 8 Voucher Users
articles.narrative: A housing watchdog group has accused Greystar, a major apartment owner, of widespread discrimination against Section 8 voucher holders across seven jurisdictions. The Housing Rights Initiative filed 114 complaints with state agencies and attorneys general, alleging that Greystar employees unlawfully refused to accept public assistance payments or imposed illegal conditions on their use. This marks the latest in a series of legal challenges for Greystar, which has faced similar allegations in the past and recently settled claims related to rent price-fixing and illegal fees for service members.
